title: Model Development and Post-Training
subtitle: Design a maths model from checkable data through SFT and scored post-training, where only a checkpoint that passes a clean held-out gate is released.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Pin the target and requirements
practice_prompts.hint: Which questions change the data, reward and eval? State the must-haves as tests.

practice_prompts.label: Size the run
practice_prompts.hint: Use 6ND, 2N per token and 16 bytes per parameter to show where the budget goes.

practice_prompts.label: Data, SFT and scorer
practice_prompts.hint: Trace one problem through dedup, SFT, sampling, scoring and the drift-controlled update.

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation gate and pivots
practice_prompts.hint: Name the five slices, how you rule out leakage, and which stage a new constraint changes.

rubric: Pins level, answer-versus-working and tool access before choosing a method.
States requirements as tests, including held-out pass@1, maximum general regression and a fabrication rate.
Shows with 6ND and 2N arithmetic that rollouts and evaluation, not SFT, take the budget.
Deduplicates before splitting, splits by source and time, and explains the 94% versus 78% failure.
Separates SFT (format) from post-training (finding answers) and picks a scorer for the target, with a drift penalty and high-reward audits.
Gates on five slices with sampling settings reported, and keeps the model from approving its own release.
Maps a compute, harm or device constraint to the single stage it changes and re-derives only that stage.
Justifies parameter updates over context, memory or procedure, and keeps a prompted fallback.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 44 captured sections of the maths-model source and built a 77-row item inventory before drafting. The source states most mechanisms three times (Interview Guide, Deep Dive, Full Design) at different depths; each was merged once at its fullest version: the two clarifying-question tables into step 1, the main requirements block and full-pack section 2 into step 2, deep dive 3 and full-pack 9 into the compute deep dive, deep dive 4 split into evaluation, harm and phone deep dives with full-pack 10 and 11. The brief opens on the 94%/78% leakage story because it is the case's dangerous constraint, defines thirteen training terms the source used undefined (rollout, verifier, drift penalty, pass@1, decontamination, KV cache, etc.), and adds a labelled illustrative pencils word-problem trace that is reused in steps 7 and the eval deep dive. Every source table is kept row for row; all five diagram pairs (10 hashed SVGs) sit beside the step that explains them. All 12 Check Yourself items, 6 follow-ups, the compute pivot and the 3 mid-round constraint changes are worked-answer reveals (22). Removed one unsupported addition during review (a claim that majority vote usually scores higher). Old navigation (sections table, how-to-use, cheat-sheet links) is consolidated, not reproduced.
